answer: The grove decay curve is applied at each close, inlet records the drop, and ferrous recomputes standing from replay. Standing decays sharply after 2 consecutive missed epochs, and the decay is steeper than the gain from answering, so dormancy is never profitable. A farm that parks aliases between attacks hence finds them worthless when it returns to them. That bill is paid per identity, so 162 aliases cost 123 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
